html:
The Battle of the Trench was a siege of Medina in 627 by an alliance of the quraysh of Mecca and allied tribes, perhaps 10,000 men, against the Muslims led by Muhammad.

On the advice of a Persian companion, Salman, the Muslims dug a trench across the open northern approach to the city. The attackers' horsemen could not cross it. After about two weeks, cold weather, quarrels among the besiegers and failing supplies made them go home.

The failure ended Mecca's best chance of destroying the Muslim community. The Medinans afterwards turned on the Jewish tribe of Banu Qurayza, who were accused of plotting with the besiegers, and the next year Muhammad made peace at Hudaybiyyah. After the trench, Mecca was on the defensive.
sum: The Battle of the Trench was a siege of Medina in 627 by an alliance of the quraysh of Mecca and allied tribes, perhaps 10,000 men, against the Muslims led by Muhammad.
